steps.content: Someone looks out of place... well, you've long since gotten used to it.
After a few pauses along the way, you finally arrive at your destination. Yet the sight before you...

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: It should be... right? That's what our astronomer said.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Boss, are you sure you didn't read the map wrong?

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: No way. Not a chance. I never make the same mistake twice.
Blue. Nothing but blue.
The water here is the clearest you've ever seen, cleaner even than the swimming pools in Eastside's posh mansions.
You can even make out every single pebble and strand of seaweed on the seabed.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: ...Doesn't look like there's any Mania here.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: No, this isn't right. Something's missing here.
The grill master is the first to spot the problem.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Fish.
An idea strikes the ever-resourceful boss next to you.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Hey, that reminds me... There's an old Eastian saying: "Water that's too pure has no fish."

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Maybe this isn't the sea. That's why there are no fish.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: Then the answer is obvious.
Dreya steps forward and dips her hand into the water. The surface boils at her touch. The currents come alive, and the entire space seems to wake. Bai Yi, taken by surprise, steps back instinctively.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: H-huh? No, wait, I was just kidding!
Before she can finish her words, the water at your feet towers into a colossal wave, its enormous shadow engulfing you all.
(Scene change)
Bai Yi's voice still rings in your ears as you find yourself deep under the sea.
Your vision is consumed by an absolute darkness. At first, you see nothing, only a chilling void.
Slowly, your eyes adjust to the unknown space. Your feet touch the ground. The water doesn't flood your lungs; it feels no different from standing on dry land.
But the "land" here is incredibly heavy. The omnipresent seawater is no longer a gentle medium. You can only feel your way along the seafloor rock, inching forward until you reach a wider clearing.
Heehee...
A giggle cuts through the dense water and pierces your eardrums. The aura of Mania surges and churns with her voice.
It's a blurry silhouette, slender and twisted, almost one with the sea.
Just you? You're not nearly enough...
You strain your eyes, and by the faint, dying glow of plankton, you finally make out the shape of the space.

In a clearing surrounded by jagged reefs, several old school desks and chairs lie about. They clearly don't belong in the ocean. The wood is black and rotten, covered in slimy seaweed and barnacles, their metal parts rusted through.
And slumped in one of the seats, head hung low, is the astronomer who first touched the water.
That feeling of dissonance hits you again.
Even if she were dragged into a Mania's domain, someone with Dreya's power shouldn't have been captured this easily. She wouldn't have acted so rashly, either. What's happening to her...?
Look... another one's here! I always find them. I always do!
It drifts closer to Dreya, as if declaring its victory. The Mania in the space throbs with its words.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: ...You can't... hurt me...
...Hahahaha! Don't tell me you're scared?
The shadow quivers with excitement, spreading its arms as it slowly approaches the astronomer.
This is an emergency. You have to use the shackles. Even in this virtual space, a Mania incarnate has terrifying destructive power.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Hiyah! Take this, Mania!
But just as the shackles are about to activate, two figures tear through the darkness like lightning, fierce currents streaming behind them as they land perfectly between the shadow and Dreya.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: Let her go.
The long blade gleams with a cold light as it slashes at the shadow. At the same time, a shock grenade detonates on its other side.
The clash you expected happens, but soon, you realize something is off...
The shadow doesn't shriek in agony or fight back with feral rage as you'd expect from a Mania incarnate.
Instead, it just looks... stunned?

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: See? I told you. You can't hurt me.
The supposed kidnapping victim gets up, gesturing for Bai Yi and Jane to stop. They look at Dreya, confused, then back at the figure they just sent flying...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Cough... cough cough...

steps.speaker: Bai Yi & Jane
steps.content: Huh?
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Whoops... Talk about a misunderstanding. Friendly fire, huh?
Bai Yi scratches her head sheepishly. Next to her, Jane nods so fast that she looks like a nervous woodpecker.
Lamia, their unfortunate target, is laden with an armful of Whitestone Industries' merchandise, from toothpaste, toothbrushes, snacks, to business cards, all part of Bai Yi's apology package.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: So, you're not the source of Mania here.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: How could you even think it was me?!

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: Then how did this place end up like this?
The endless night, the eerie underwater world... None of this is supposed to be here.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: There's no way this is natural, right? If it is, I'm starting the hype on DisMyth right now.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: No. Someone made it this way.
Just as you're all racking your brains, Lamia speaks up hesitantly:

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Um... actually...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I got here earlier than you did. The place wasn't like this at first. It changed... a few days ago? Yeah, that's right! A few days ago!
At these words, even Bai Yi starts paying serious attention.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: It was just a normal tourist spot at first. The view was great, and night came and went like it should.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But after a few days, everything changed... I thought the Bureau was behind it at first, but now, I guess not.

steps.speaker: Option
options: You remember all that pretty clearly.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: That's because... because...
Lamia mumbles, unable to go on.
Right when she's about to reveal a crucial clue, Lamia gets cold feet.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: No! I can't say it! It's too embarrassing!

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Don't worry, all my employees at Whitestone Industries are professionally trained. No matter how funny it is, we will keep a straight face.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: That's right.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I failed my exam at the Bureau, so they sent me out on this mission early!
Your eyes fall on an exam paper on the desk, covered in red X marks.
You remember that the Bureau held a general knowledge exam last week. It wasn't difficult; half the questions were common sense.
Perhaps you've been too focused on Hella and forgotten that this former Ocean Messenger of the Thaumas Society lacks basic everyday knowledge.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Aaah... I said it out loud... I want to die of embarrassment... I just wanted to study here quietly for a retake, and then this happens!

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I found this thing on the beach, it looked like some kind of astrolabe. I thought it looked cool, so I brought it with me. Then I got trapped here and couldn't get out...
She slumps over the desk in defeat, recounting her story in a mumble.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I kept wishing someone could take the exam for me, or at least teach me what I needed to know...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But I didn't know it would be you guys! Aaaagh!
The light fades from Lamia's eyes. At this point, she has nothing left to lose.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: The astrolabe. Where is it?
While the rest of you are busy stifling laughter at Lamia's predicament, Dreya steps forward and takes her hand.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: W-what?
The sudden gesture makes Lamia jump. The Dreya you know wouldn't do something like this.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: The astrolabe.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...It's over there.
Lamia points to a desk cluttered with study materials, where a worn astrolabe is illuminated by several glowing patches of moss.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: Found it...
Dreya beckons gently, and the astrolabe flies into her palm, as if it had come to life.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...Huh?
As Lamia stares in amazement, the underwater illusion that has trapped her for days shatters, and solid ground appears beneath your feet once more.
(Scene change)
By the time the Mania is dealt with, it's already dusk.
Everyone's debating what to get for dinner, where to unwind. Even Bai Yi has changed back into her old clothes now that the threat is gone.
Only Dreya stands apart, staring at the astrolabe in her hands, lost in thought.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Hey, is that thing really so special?

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: It is. This is the source of the Mania.

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Huh? Wait... what? Am I hearing you right?
Her blunt answer leaves everyone stunned. Didn't the Mania just disappear?

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: And... I remember now. I'm part of it too.
Before anyone can process this, she drops another bombshell.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: Don't be afraid... The truth is simple.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: The Mania spilling out of this place came from Dreya. And I... I am a fragment of "her" consciousness from a specific point in time, given form by the Mania.
As "Dreya" says this, her eyes are fixed on the sea and where it meets the sky. You realize at once which point in time she comes from.
All the inconsistencies, all the little things that felt off... they all make sense now. Why she's still so fascinated by the stars, why she's acting unlike the Dreya you know.
She only remembers her original mission. Everything else is a blank.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: Please... forget me.

steps.speaker: Jane
steps.content: But... we opened a shop together.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You didn't take my exam for me, but... you taught me how to answer those questions!

steps.speaker: Bai Yi
steps.content: Right! We went surfing, we did all that cool stuff together! No way we're forgetting that!

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: ...I don't deny any of it, but I'm not the whole of her.
The sea breeze tousles her long hair, but her gaze remains fixed on the horizon.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: If the Mania continues to expand, these endless waters will spill out of this space... and drown all of DisCity.

steps.speaker: Dreya
steps.content: Now that I remember, it's time for Dreya to fulfill the true purpose she came here for.
With that, the scholar walks forward. You reach out, trying to stop her, but she only shakes her head.
A red light engulfs the sky, and her with it.

steps.speaker: Player
steps.content: Dreya!
